description: Spell-check a PubMed search query against NCBI ESpell and get the corrected query back. Use after a zero-hit or thin `pubmed_search_articles` result, or when a drug, gene, disease, or author name may be misspelled. Corrections are applied in place, so field tags, operators, spacing, and gene symbols stay as written (`alzhiemer diseese treatmnt outcomse` → `alzheimer disease treatment outcomes`). The value of an indexed field — MeSH, publication type, journal, author, language, subset, and the like (`aged[mh]`, `free full text[sb]`, `zhang y[au]`) — is kept as written, misspelled or not, since the ESpell dictionary is not the index that field searches; free-text fields such as `[tiab]`, `[ti]`, and `[tw]` are corrected. Words in all capitals, with digits or non-ASCII letters, or differing only in case are never changed, nor is a single letter swapped for another (`q fever`, the initial in `smith q`), words after a number or symbol ESpell skips are left as written, and `hasSuggestion` is false when no correction was applied. Each correction is checked against PubMed first: one with under a tenth of the PubMed records of the word it replaces is dropped and the word kept (`tirzepatide`, which ESpell would turn into `irzepatide`), unless ESpell's MeSH dictionary offers a spelling PubMed holds more often than the word (`tirzepatid` → `tirzepatide`). A check that cannot run leaves ESpell's correction applied, or the dropped word as written, and `notice` names it. Re-run the search with `corrected`.

query.description: PubMed search query to spell-check. Must carry a term: a value of only whitespace or invisible characters, such as a zero-width space, is rejected rather than sent to ESpell.

name: pubmed_spell_check

corrected.description: The query with ESpell's accepted corrections applied in place; field tags, the values of indexed fields such as `aged[mh]` and `zhang y[au]`, operators, spacing, words in capitals or with digits, and a single letter ESpell would swap for another are kept as written. So is a word whose ESpell correction has under a tenth of its PubMed records, unless ESpell's MeSH dictionary offers a spelling PubMed holds more often than the word, which is used instead. Same as `original` when `hasSuggestion` is false.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `queue_full`: The local NCBI request queue shed the call — the queue is full, or the call cannot start before its total deadline (for example behind the cooldown that follows an NCBI 429). `ncbi_unreachable`: NCBI E-utilities failed on every attempt the retry budget allowed — no connection, no answer within the per-request timeout, an HTTP 5xx other than 501 and 504, or a backend failure NCBI reported in its response — and the call stopped there: retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap, or the call made one attempt without retrying because the previous call to the same E-utility had failed on every attempt. `ncbi_rate_limited`: NCBI answered HTTP 429 (too many requests) and the call stopped on it — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap. `ncbi_deadline_exceeded`: The deadline for the NCBI call expired before NCBI answered successfully — mid-request, while queued, during a retry backoff, or before the next request could be sent. That deadline is the total NCBI request deadline, or the time the tool call had left when that was shorter; `deadlineMs` names its length. `ncbi_timed_out`: NCBI answered HTTP 504 (gateway timeout), 408 (request timeout), or 425 (too early) and the call stopped on it — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap. `ncbi_invalid_response`: NCBI returned a body that could not be parsed (invalid XML/JSON), or a well-formed document that is not the answer the request asked for (no result element, or an ESearch result with no numeric count). `ncbi_resource_not_found`: NCBI returned a structured "not found" error for the requested ID(s). `blank_query`: The query contains no search term: nothing is left once whitespace and invisible characters such as a zero-width space are disregarded. pubmed_search_articles and pubmed_europepmc_search first decode HTML entities and also disregard markup and parentheses, so `()`, ``, and ` ` hold no term there; pubmed_search_articles also disregards bracketed field tags such as `[pdat]`. On pubmed_search_articles an exactly-empty `query` is not blank: it means no query, and the search runs on its filters. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

hasSuggestion.description: Whether at least one correction was applied to `corrected`

notice.description: Names each correction applied as ESpell wrote it without its PubMed record-count check, and each word kept as written without a MeSH-dictionary spelling tried, with the cause: an NCBI request failed, the checks reached their limit of 12 requests, or they ran out of time (10 seconds, or less when the tool call had less time left). Absent when every check ran.

title: Pubmed Spell Check
